en: The names of fifteen hundred Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions, together with various Buddhas bearing the same title,
"Able to Wound" (Nengshang), are as follows: if one can, even once, prostrate oneself with the five limbs touching the ground and pay homage, with one's own mouth...
I now universally prostrate to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
I now universally prostrate to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time up to a thousand times.
Only after that did he arise.
The merit obtained is as described above.
Next, there are fifty-three Buddhas who appear in the *Bhaiṣajyarāja-bhaiṣajyasamudgata-sūtra*.
If any son or daughter of good family, as well as all other sentient beings,
should hear the names of these fifty-three Buddhas,
such persons shall not fall into the evil realms for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas.
Furthermore, if there are those who can recite the names of these fifty-three Buddhas,
they shall always encounter the Buddhas of the ten directions in every place where they are born.
Moreover, if there are those who can reverently prostrate to the fifty-three Buddhas with a sincere heart, [they shall likewise attain such merit].
The four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, and the slandering of the Vaipulya sutras are all completely purified,
by virtue of the original vows of all Buddhas.
In every moment of thought, one immediately attains the eradication of all such sins as those mentioned above.
[This applies to] the Buddha Universal Radiance and the Buddha Universal Illumination.

Next, there are the Buddhas of thirty directions from the *Niyatavinīśaya-sūtra*.
If there is a bodhisattva...
One incurs the five sins of immediate retribution by committing [sexual misconduct] with a woman or with a man.
Or there may be those who commit offenses with their hands, offenses against stupas, or offenses against the Sangha,
as well as other such offenses; a bodhisattva should, in the presence of the thirty-five Buddhas, [confess them].
For whatever grave offenses one has committed, one should dwell alone day and night and repent with a sincere mind.
As for the method of repentance: take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Sangha. Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha.

To all such Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in all worlds,
who eternally abide in the world.
May these World-Honored Ones hold me in their compassionate thoughts,
whether in this life or in previous lives.
Whatever various sins one has committed since beginningless saṃsāra— whether committed by oneself,
incited in others, or rejoiced in as they were committed;
whether regarding a stūpa, the Saṅgha, or the property of the Saṅgha from the four quarters.
Whether taking [the property] oneself or instructing others to take it, seeing it taken and rejoicing in it;
or committing the grave offenses of the five *ānantarya* crimes,
whether doing so oneself or instructing others to do so, seeing it done and rejoicing in it.
Regarding the karmic obstructions of the ten unwholesome paths of action— whether committed by oneself, taught to others,
witnessed being committed, or rejoiced in—
and whether they were concealed or not.

Or, if one does not conceal [one's faults], one should fall into the hells, the realm of hungry ghosts, the animal realm, and other evil destinies; into the borderlands, among the low-born, or as a Mleccha.
Such are the karmic obstructions created in these various places.
I now repent of them all.
May the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, bear witness to me now;
may they hold me in their mindful remembrance.
Furthermore, before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
he spoke these words:
"Whether in this life or in other lives..."
They have practiced giving,
or maintained pure precepts,
even to the extent of bestowing a single morsel of food upon an animal.
Or they cultivate pure conduct;
with all roots of goodness, they bring sentient beings to maturity,
and with all roots of goodness, they practice for enlightenment.
All roots of goodness and unsurpassed wisdom—
all these roots of goodness, taken together, calculated, and weighed—
are entirely dedicated toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Just as all Buddhas of the past, future, and present have performed dedication, so do I likewise dedicate.
Next, there are the thirty-eight Buddhas of the six directions from the *Sūtra on the Dharma Upheld by All Buddhas: A Praise of Amitābha*.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
in the eastern direction there is a Buddha named Akṣobhya Tathāgata and Sumerudhvaja Tathāgata.
Mahāmeru Tathāgata, Meruprabhāsa Tathāgata, and Karuṇānanda Tathāgata.
In the southern direction there is a Buddha named Candrasūryapradīpa Tathāgata,
Prabhāsa-nāma Tathāgata, and Mahājvālā-gotra Tathāgata.
The Tathāgata Sumerudīpa; the Tathāgata Amitavīrya;
and in the western direction, there is a Buddha named Amitāyus Tathāgata.
Tathāgata Immeasurable Banner,
Tathāgata Immeasurable Pennant,
and Tathāgata Great Radiance.
The Tathāgata Universal Great Radiance,
the Tathāgata Jewel Banner,
and the Tathāgata Pure Radiance.
In the north, there are Buddhas named Tathāgata Great Flame Kindred,
Tathāgata Joyful Sound, and Tathāgata Unconquerable.
From the Tathāgata Sūryodaya and the Tathāgata Ratnajālaprabha,
there is a Buddha in the direction below named... [name].
The Tathāgata Siṃha; the Tathāgata Dūrasamantajayaśas; the Tathāgata Yaśaḥprabha.

the Tathāgata Dharmadhvaja,

Most Fragrant Tathāgata,
and Star-King Tathāgata.
Tathāgata Fragrant Radiance;

Tathāgata King of Wondrous Fragrance Trees,
Tathāgata Jewel Lotus Flower,
and Tathāgata Who Instructs in All Matters.
Tathāgata Sumerumati.
If any son or daughter of good family hears the names of these Buddhas from this sutra, [they shall attain such merit].
These beings shall be protected and sustained by all Buddhas;
they will certainly attain the stage of non-retrogression and shall realize the unsurpassed, right, and true path.
In this way, Śāriputra,
with single-minded faith and joy,
you should widely proclaim and disseminate it.
Practice this with a sincere heart.
If there should be anyone who upholds my name,
or who holds and cherishes these names and titles of the aforementioned Buddhas, [they shall attain liberation].
Taking this merit, one should with a sincere heart vow to be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
If one has made such a vow in the past...
If those who now make this vow desire to be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha,
these beings shall certainly attain the stage of non-retrogression.
When these individuals pass away, they shall all be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
if there are good men or good women—
Those who wish to attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha should always,
with a sincere heart, recollect Amitābha Buddha and the names of the Buddhas of the six directions mentioned above.
They should single-mindedly pay respectful homage without interruption.
Next are the five directions.
From the eastern direction up to the zenith,
there are one hundred and thirty-nine Buddhas.
It appears in the *Sarvabuddhaguṇavyūha-sūtra*.
This *Sarvabuddhaguṇavyūha-sūtra* consists of two fascicles, totaling fifty-five and a half pages.
Each page contains twenty-five lines.
The practice consists of seventeen characters.

In the eastern direction is the Buddha Infinite Multitude King, whose body is like a precious image of flowing lapis lazuli light amidst lotuses, adorned with a topknot of all ornaments and the radiance of the world-transcending light of supreme fragrances; his eyes are pure and equal, delighting in the marks of virtue, and he is the sovereign of infinite suns and moons who fulfills all vows, accomplishes sublime transformations, and adorns the entire *dharmadhātu*.
In that [assembly] there was a bodhisattva named Anupama (Incomparable).

He received the prediction that he would next attain buddhahood under the name Phantasmal Sound Blazing Variegated Flower Light Jewel Red Lotus Golden Flame Body Manifestly Soft Unobstructed Eye Radiating Light Throughout the Ten Directions Pervading All Phenomena King Buddha.
In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas equal in number to the atoms within hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, all bearing the same name, Samantaprabha.

In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas equal in number to the atoms within eight thousand unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, all bearing the same name, Samantabhadra.
In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas named Universal Victory (*Samjaya*), numbering as many as the atoms in ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayuta* Buddha-fields.
In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas named Worthy Head (*Bhadramukha*), numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakable Buddha-fields.
In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields, all bearing the same name, Vajragarbha.
In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in one million buddha-fields, all bearing the same name, Vajraketu.

in each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand Buddha-lands, all bearing the same name, Samantaguṇa.
There are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand Buddha-lands, all bearing the same name, Victorious Realm (Jinjingjie).

In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten thousand Buddha-fields, all sharing the same name, Dharmamati.
In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields, all sharing the same name, Samantadhvajavikrāmin.
In each of the ten directions, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-lands, all bearing the same name, Wondrous Dharma Buddha;

and twenty trillion Buddhas, all bearing the same name, King of Majestic Sound Buddha.

twenty billion Buddhas, all sharing the same name Cloud-Sovereign-Lamp-King;

one hundred [Buddhas] shared the same name, Sandalwood Ocean Buddha;
and thirty trillion [Buddhas] shared the same name, Puṣya Buddha.

twenty thousand buddhas were all named Candrasūryapradīpa;
and twenty thousand buddhas were all named Maṇiprabha.

Forty [Buddhas] were identical in name as Ratnaketu-prabhāsa-rāja;
forty [Buddhas] were identical in name as Mahābala-ghoṣarāja;
thirty [Buddhas] were identical in name as Prabhāsa-garbha.
Thirty [Buddhas] were all named Padmagandhabalavardhana;
twenty were all named Acintyarāja; and twenty were all named Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña.
Fifteen were equally named Jñānagiri-dhvaja Buddha;
fifteen were equally named Sūryaprabha Buddha;
eleven were equally named Vivṛta-dharmaghoṣa Buddha.
Ten [Buddhas] sharing the same name, Radiance Free from Sound;
nine [Buddhas] sharing the same name, Wisdom Radiance;
and nine [Buddhas] sharing the same name, King of Merit and Dharma Renown.
Eight [Buddhas] shared the same name, Ghoṣeśvara;
eight shared the same name, Vigatabhayābhayaśrīrāja;
and seven shared the same name, Acintyaghoṣa.
Four were named Tathāgata Dragon Sovereign;
three were named Tathāgata Lion’s Play;
and three were named Tathāgata Wisdom Treasury.
Two [Buddhas] were identical in name as Sūryaprabha Buddha;
two were identical in name as Jñānabodhigiripuṣparāja Buddha;
and two were identical in name as Guṇaparvatajñānabodhi Buddha.
Two were both named Vajrasimha Buddha;
two were both named Śīlaprabhāsa Buddha;
and two were both named Vṛddhidarśana Buddha.
Two [Buddhas] were both named Anantajñānagiri;
two were both named Ratnaprabhāsa;
and two were both named Vimalajñāna.
Two [Buddhas] with the same name, Lion-Call Buddha;
two with the same name, King of Universal Virtue Buddha;
and two with the same name, Rain of Dharma Flowers Buddha.
Two [Buddhas] with the same name: Samudravyūhaguṇarāja-jñānasamavasaraṇa Buddha;
two [Buddhas] with the same name: Guṇabala-sālarāja Buddha;
two [Buddhas] with the same name: Aparimitaguṇasāgarajñānavardhana Buddha.
Second, the Buddhas of the eon of the Merit of Identical Names:
Vajrasimhavikrīḍita Buddha, and Suvyavasthitaguṇaratnarāja Buddha.
The Buddha Universal Radiance Mountain King of Merit;
the Buddha Supreme Samādhi Abundant Adornment King;
and the Buddha Prabhūtaratna.
The Names of One Thousand Five Hundred Buddhas Currently Residing in the Ten Directions,
along with Various Buddhas Sharing the Same Name, including Ratnottama Buddha, Mṛdukara-dhvaja-satyaghoṣarāja Buddha; one fascicle.
